title: Why Attention Beats Money at Work | Principles of Management Ep 11
description:
Ravi pays his Chai Corner team well, but the team is quiet and the chai is slow. More money changes nothing. Then one evening he sits down and listens, and the next morning the team works faster. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai stall to understand Elton Mayo's human relations approach, step by step.

You will meet Elton Mayo, the Australian-born Harvard Business School professor, and see how Taylor's view of workers as parts of a machine differs from Mayo's view of workers as people. We walk through the Hawthorne studies at Western Electric's Hawthorne Works near Chicago (1924 to 1932) stage by stage: the lighting tests, the relay test room, about 20,000 interviews and the bank wiring room. Then we sum up the four lessons, including the Hawthorne effect, and see recognition, listening, belonging, informal groups and care beyond money at work today. We also look at the limits honestly: the studies were small and poorly controlled, and when economists found the old lighting data in 2011, the effect was much smaller than the legend.

This is Episode 11 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
